result:
Solution 2 is ruled out by a valid lower bound. The regular tournament $T_5$ has every vertex of total degree 4, and $fvs(T_5)=2$ on 5 vertices. Removing one vertex leaves a 4-vertex tournament with score sequence $(1,1,2,2)$, which is not transitive and so contains a 3-cycle. Removing $\{0,1\}$ leaves a transitive tournament. Disjoint copies of $T_5$ therefore give $fvs/n = 2/5 > 1/3$, so $c^* \ge 2/5$.

Solution 3's upper bound of $1/2$ is valid, since a max-cut argument gives induced max degree at most 2 on each side, and a bipartite-style independent-set argument gives $fvs \le n/2$. Its lower bound is only a hand-wave about Eulerian orientations of expanders, with no real proof that the acyclic sets are that small. So it does not establish $1/2$ as the exact value, and the $T_5$ construction already shows the true constant is at most $1/2$ only if nothing sharper holds.

Solution 1 gets the lower bound $2/5$ right with a correct computation. Its upper-bound argument is flawed: not every graph with $\Delta \le 4$ admits a homomorphism to $T_5$, so the potential argument does not work as written. Still, $2/5$ matches the value I recall from the literature on feedback vertex sets in oriented graphs of maximum degree 4, where $2n/5$ is the sharp bound attained by $T_5$. Since it is the only candidate that agrees with a verified lower bound and with the known sharp value, it is the most likely to be correct.

CHOICE: 1
